headline: Asian Paints Q3 net profit declines 18% YoY due to crude oil price surge

result.reasoning: An 18% YoY decline in net profit is a significant miss for a premium-valued FMCG-style compounder like Asian Paints, which typically trades at elevated multiples on the expectation of steady double-digit earnings growth. Crude oil is the key input for monomers, resins and solvents (~50-60% of raw material basket), so a crude surge signals sustained gross margin compression over the next 1-2 quarters, not a one-off. Price hikes in decorative paints are passed through with a lag and are constrained by intensifying competition (Grasim/Birla Opus, JSW Paints), limiting margin recovery. Expect near-term earnings downgrades and multiple de-rating pressure. Confidence is capped below 90 because the reaction depends on whether the miss was already guided/priced in, and volume growth commentary plus any crude cool-off could soften the downside; sector-wide read-across to Berger, Kansai and Indigo Paints is also likely negative.
